b4662f78d75abf170a70c791fc4355d3dcdabc64.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and basal cell degeneration, are consistent with lichen planus. ba916d252ea0f7b76f749096fbca29a4cad252c6.rationale: The presence of two heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, along with the clinical findings of elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and open iridocorneal angle, supports this diagnosis.

bab0ec7258dff88d7c7b17b50d295ea46d4f46a5.rationale: The patient's ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI results all point towards a diagnosis of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy, with evidence of global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, dilated RV, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall, which are characteristic findings of this condition.

rejected.label: Ventricular Tachycardia

bd6bde6deafd7ecb52567963741a531a40feee8c.rationale: The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and mucin-containing goblet cells, without cytologic atypia or atypical mitotic figures, is consistent with Schneiderian Papilloma.

rejected.label: Inverted Papilloma
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma typically shows endophytic growth pattern, which is not described in the histologic examination.

rejected.label: Verrucous Carcinoma
rejected.why: Verrucous carcinoma typically shows keratinizing squamous epithelium, which contradicts the nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium in the histologic examination.

rejected.label: Papillomatosis

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma typically shows cytologic atypia and atypical mitotic figures, which are not present in the histologic examination.

c18275f68da391ae20b3256188a4535154ad9091.rationale: The patient's presentation with multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion, along with immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1, is consistent with malignant pleural mesothelioma. The disease's stability after treatment and subsequent development of a nodular growth on the tongue, which showed neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: The presence of epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures and immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1 does not support a desmoplastic subtype, which typically has a more sarcomatoid appearance.

rejected.label: Sarcomatoid malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor showed epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures, which is not consistent with the sarcomatoid subtype, which typically has a more spindle cell appearance.

rejected.label: Biphasic malignant mesothelioma
rejected.why: There is no mention of both epithelioid and sarcomatoid components in the tumor, which is required for a biphasic diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor showed immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1, which is consistent with mesothelioma, not epithelioid hemangioendothelioma.

c1e64aa579fb6ecb83f90ba47a0509be179c1403.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques that began as pustules, along with histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia, exocytosis of neutrophils, and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, is consistent with Sweet syndrome. The presence of microabscesses scattered with eosinophils and the lack of granulomas or multinucleated giant cells also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can present with painful ulcers, the histopathology typically shows a more pronounced neutrophilic infiltrate and the presence of granulomas, which are not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
rejected.why: Erythema elevatum diutinum is characterized by chronic, symmetric, and palpable purpura, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of acute, painful plaques.

rejected.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: Generalized pustular psoriasis typically presents with widespread pustules on an erythematous base, and the histopathology shows a more pronounced epidermal hyperplasia and parakeratosis, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis
rejected.why: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis is a condition that presents with fever, neutrophilia, and a characteristic dermatosis, but the patient's presentation and histopathology are more consistent with Sweet syndrome.

c4598e2a51b628135cf6377cc953ddaad5d0d4c8.rationale: The patient's presentation of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face, particularly on the medial cheeks, chin, and nose, along with the histopathology showing intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation, is most consistent with papulopustular rosacea. The exacerbation by sunlight exposure and the failure to respond to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms worsen with sunlight exposure, the specific pattern of pustular eruptions and the lack of other typical features such as burning sensation or blistering make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more widespread and itchy lesions, and the patient's lack of significant pruritus and the specific histopathological findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Actinic prurigo
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic intense pruritus or the specific distribution of lesions typically seen in actinic prurigo.

rejected.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows subcorneal pustule formation, the clinical presentation and the lack of other typical features such as flexural involvement or the presence of systemic symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.

c497f63d5a2ecbc23428a54dffbe7411bfe90ef8.rationale: The patient's presentation with abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and 'bruises' on both flanks that progressed to purpuric retiform patches, along with laboratory findings of hyponatremia, neutropenia, elevated liver enzymes, and positive tissue culture and Gram staining showing Gram-positive cocci, is most consistent with Purpura fulminans, a condition characterized by rapid progression of hemorrhagic necrosis of the skin and is often associated with severe infections.

rejected.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
rejected.why: While Neisseria meningitidis can cause severe sepsis and purpura, the Gram staining showing Gram-positive cocci does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: Although Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome can present with severe systemic symptoms and skin manifestations, the specific findings of purpuric retiform patches and the laboratory results do not exclusively point to this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Meningococcemia
rejected.why: Meningococcemia typically presents with a petechial or purpuric rash, but the Gram-positive cocci on tissue Gram staining do not align with Neisseria meningitidis, which is Gram-negative.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome can cause severe systemic illness, the presence of purpuric retiform patches and the specific laboratory findings, including the type of organisms seen on Gram stain, are more indicative of Purpura fulminans.

c5ad84298a12ceadee524e4e18db66c92487063f.rationale: The presence of angiofibroma-like facial papules, history of renal transplant suggesting possible renal angiomyolipoma, and the specific finding of crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblast cytoplasm on electron microscopy are highly suggestive of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, especially given the age of onset and the combination of skin and potential renal involvement.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic lung cysts, renal cell carcinoma, or other specific features of Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome in the vignette

rejected.label: Lipoid Proteinosis

rejected.label: Fibrous Papule of the Face
rejected.why: While the biopsy shows features compatible with an angiofibroma, the presence of crystalline inclusions and the patient's broader clinical picture suggest a more complex syndrome than a solitary fibrous papule

rejected.label: Multiple Hereditary Exostoses
rejected.why: The primary features of this condition are multiple osteochondromas, which are not mentioned in the vignette; the conical-shaped teeth could be a feature of several conditions and are not specific enough to support this diagnosis alone

c90acb7715869ab89754533ff42d3295931d9c57.rationale: The histopathologic examination showing bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium and villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia is consistent with onychomatricoma, a rare benign tumor of the nail matrix.

ca48b17aea27ffe0bbb1d69262c9d3cad9939518.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including incomplete closure of the right eye, flattening of the right nasolabial fold, and right-sided hemiplegia, are consistent with a thalamic hemorrhage, which is supported by the CT scan showing hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle.

rejected.label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
rejected.why: While the patient does have an intracerebral hemorrhage, the specific location in the thalamus suggests a more specific diagnosis of thalamic hemorrhage.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: The presence of hemorrhage on the CT scan rules out ischemic stroke as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest cerebral amyloid angiopathy, such as multiple lobar hemorrhages or a history of dementia.

rejected.label: Hypertensive encephalopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a localized lesion, such as a thalamic hemorrhage, rather than a diffuse process like hypertensive encephalopathy.

ca94d08f9769b7e8e63661cc99d3c90c95f30796.rationale: The patient's presentation of left-sided neck pain, neck stiffness, headache, and pyrexia, combined with the laboratory confirmation of F necrophorum infection and imaging findings of an intramuscular abscess, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lemierre's syndrome
rejected.why: Lemierre's syndrome typically involves septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein and distant septic emboli, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Parapharyngeal abscess
rejected.why: The location of the abscess in the left paraspinal musculature, as shown on CT and MRI, does not correspond to the typical location of a parapharyngeal abscess.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal abscess
rejected.why: The microbiological culture identified F necrophorum, not Staphylococcus, as the causative organism.

rejected.label: Pyomyositis
rejected.why: While pyomyositis is a muscle infection that could present similarly, the specific identification of F necrophorum infection makes it a more precise diagnosis in this case.

cc34dbe9a19b8187eeae1430f3e20773908eddab.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, generalized eruption, and target lesions, along with the presence of bullae and mucosal involvement, is consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. The recent history of photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and the positive autoantibody profile also support this diagnosis, as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome can be triggered by systemic lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: While the patient has widespread skin lesions and bullae, the presence of target lesions and the lack of extensive epidermal detachment make Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis less likely.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, the current presentation is more consistent with a specific cutaneous manifestation, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, rather than a flare of systemic lupus erythematosus itself.

rejected.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and the presence of typical lesions of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus are noted, but the current presentation with target lesions, bullae, and systemic symptoms is more suggestive of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

rejected.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has bullae, the overall clinical presentation and the presence of target lesions are more consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome than bullous lupus erythematosus.

cc93423190ab76386f5fe3342eea87b0e8e1dd1f.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, dizziness, nausea, and moderate tetraparesis, are consistent with brainstem involvement. The positive Romberg test and the presence of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum on MRI also support this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient's symptoms and MRI findings are more consistent with an inflammatory or autoimmune process, such as Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis, rather than an infectious process like meningitis.

rejected.label: Listeria Meningitis
rejected.why: The patient's cerebrospinal fluid culture was positive, but the clinical presentation and MRI findings are not typical for Listeria Meningitis

rejected.label: Cryptococcal Meningitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including the cerebrospinal fluid analysis, do not suggest a fungal infection like Cryptococcal Meningitis

rejected.label: Tuberculous Meningitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including the cerebrospinal fluid analysis and MRI, do not suggest a chronic infection like Tuberculous Meningitis

rejected.label: Brainstem Encephalitis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms and MRI findings suggest brainstem involvement, Bickerstaff Brainstem Encephalitis is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's clinical presentation

cd19d7a2da9622fecc3b17fb27b9f880a3c11fe9.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with symptoms such as progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, supports this diagnosis. The severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging also aligns with frontotemporal dementia, particularly given the genetic finding.

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: While vertical gaze palsy is a hallmark of progressive supranuclear palsy, the genetic finding of a TBK1 pathogenic variant and the broader range of symptoms better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia. The specific genetic finding points more precisely to TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: Although tongue atrophy and pyramidal signs could suggest amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the absence of clear evidence of widespread motor neuron involvement and the presence of cognitive impairment and vertical gaze palsy make this less likely.

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: This condition often presents with asymmetric parkinsonism and alien limb syndrome, which are not mentioned in the vignette. The genetic and imaging findings better support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

cd7e594784615ca98683d4f3b2f086652b40f170.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels on skin biopsy, along with the clinical presentation of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: While possible, the specific involvement of lymphatic vessels suggests a more specific diagnosis related to lymphatic invasion.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
rejected.why: This typically presents at the time of initial cancer diagnosis, not a year later, and the clinical description does not fully align with the characteristic diffuse erythema and edema of inflammatory breast cancer.

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinoma
rejected.why: This term, while related, is less specific and does not fully capture the clinical and pathological findings presented.

rejected.label: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion
rejected.why: This option is broader and does not specifically describe the clinical presentation and biopsy findings as accurately as carcinomatous lymphangitis.

d00031535063ab15a25ee20b9a4e2077abe3dd06.rationale: The combination of progressive disorder, autonomic dysfunction (abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function and anhidrosis), ataxia, and cognitive decline without significant sensory symptoms, along with the imaging findings of bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami and global diffuse brain volume loss, are highly suggestive of Multiple System Atrophy.

rejected.label: Fabry Disease

rejected.label: Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease

rejected.why: This condition presents with progressive upper and lower motor neuron dysfunction, which is not the primary feature of this case, and the autonomic and imaging findings do not align closely with Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome

d6b4220a42afa5bfd4b83c563b571ef59b7f7178.rationale: The patient's history of COPD and complaints of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation, along with the family member witnessing him struggling for air before losing consciousness, suggest that a COPD exacerbation led to the cardiac arrest.

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of a pulmonary embolism, such as a reported DVT or sudden onset of symptoms without prior respiratory issues.

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Coronary angiography showed no acute occlusions, making myocardial infarction less likely as the primary cause of the cardiac arrest.

rejected.why: While the patient has COPD, which can lead to cor pulmonale, the information provided does not specifically indicate right-sided heart failure due to lung disease as the primary cause of the cardiac arrest.

rejected.label: Right ventricular failure
rejected.why: Although the ECG shows right axis deviation and other signs that could suggest right ventricular strain, the primary issue appears to be related to the patient's COPD exacerbation rather than isolated right ventricular failure.

d7460364d8dc9a8f70fee286e8f5ee0fe21db6e8.rationale: The patient's ECG findings show a normal sinus rhythm with a prolonged PR interval and some P waves that do not conduct to ventricles, which is consistent with Mobitz Type II Atrioventricular Block. The electrophysiology study also shows a prolonged His-ventricular interval, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG shows a normal sinus rhythm, which is not consistent with Sick Sinus Syndrome.

rejected.label: Complete Heart Block
rejected.why: The patient's ECG shows that some P waves do conduct to ventricles, which is not consistent with Complete Heart Block.

rejected.label: His-Purkinje Disease
rejected.why: While the patient's ECG shows a prolonged His-ventricular interval, this finding alone is not sufficient to diagnose His-Purkinje Disease without further evidence of disease in the His-Purkinje system.

rejected.label: Lev-Lenegre Disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and ECG findings are not typical of Lev-Lenegre Disease, which is a rare condition that typically presents with a prolonged PR interval and widening of the QRS complex in younger patients.

d7f24acd66d87e29b4fe301c937b73220472e815.rationale: The patient's histopathology results showing a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, along with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Additionally, the patient's medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and the presence of café au lait macules are also associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology results do not match the typical findings of juvenile xanthogranuloma, which is a condition the patient already has in their medical history.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical presentation are not typical for Erdheim-Chester disease, which usually affects adults and has a distinct set of systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: The patient's immunohistochemical staining results do not match the typical profile of Rosai-Dorfman disease, which is usually positive for S100 and CD1a.

rejected.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology and immunohistochemical staining results are more consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis than indeterminate cell histiocytosis, which has a more variable and nonspecific immunophenotype.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Hypertension
rejected.why: The patient has a history of moderate pulmonary hypertension, but it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the decline in left ventricular ejection fraction and the patient's current symptoms.

rejected.label: Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Although cardiomyopathy could be a possible diagnosis, the patient's presentation and decline in cardiac function are more specifically explained by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

dc66485937f9cc0c5e74c8658bce651d977cbf43.rationale: The patient's history of lupus nephritis and the presence of vacuolar interface dermatitis, follicular involvement, and epidermal atrophy on biopsy are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, which is a chronic, scarring form of cutaneous lupus erythematosus that often presents with periorbital lesions.

rejected.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus typically presents with papulosquamous or annular polycyclic lesions in a photodistributed pattern, which does not match the patient's periorbital eruption.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus is characterized by flat-topped, violaceous papules and can involve the skin and mucous membranes, but the biopsy findings and clinical presentation in this case are more consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory myopathy that presents with skin manifestations such as Gottron's papules and heliotrope rash, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus is a broad term that encompasses several subtypes, including discoid lupus erythematosus, and the patient's presentation is more specifically consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

f04ec84d1403e57fd664c79b359c2a0bb0b6f781.rationale: The patient's positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing with a 1:64 titer, along with the clinical presentation of bilateral photophobia and decreased vision, support the diagnosis of syphilitic retinitis, especially given the patient's history of multiple sexual partners with inconsistent protection.

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathology findings

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to mycosis fungoides, with potential for systemic involvement and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that encompasses mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome, with similar clinical and histopathological features

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD4, consistent with this specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, unspecified
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathology findings consistent with a peripheral T-cell lymphoma, although specific subtype cannot be determined

f9dd9f854959dfe1ed4b510ac53240cb1cb2134b.rationale: The patient's initial lesion had a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm, no ulceration, and 7 mitoses/mm2, and the BRAF V600E mutation was detected, which are all characteristic of melanoma. Additionally, the patient had lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension and locoregional recurrence with skin metastasis, which are common features of advanced melanoma.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic Melanoma
rejected.why: There is no specific mention of desmoplastic features in the histopathology report

rejected.label: Nodular Melanoma
rejected.why: The initial lesion did not have the typical features of nodular melanoma, such as a nodular shape and lack of pigment

rejected.label: Metastatic Carcinoma
rejected.why: The primary lesion was a melanocytic lesion, not a carcinoma

rejected.label: Primary Mucosal Melanoma
rejected.why: The lesion was located on the skin, not on a mucosal surface

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Block
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings and intracardiac recordings show evidence of atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and symptoms of intermittent confusion and falls, along with cardiac history, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Adams-Stokes Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Frequent pauses noted on telemetry and history of cardiac disease increase the likelihood of this condition

shortlist.label: His-Purkinje Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Intracardiac recordings showing prolongation of the His-His interval suggest involvement of the His-Purkinje system

shortlist.label: Lenegre Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and cardiac history, combined with evidence of conduction abnormalities, make this a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Prosthetic valve endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent tricuspid valve replacement and history of infective endocarditis

shortlist.label: Pulmonic valve endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Transesophageal echocardiography revealed pulmonic valve vegetations

shortlist.label: Severe tricuspid valve regurgitation
shortlist.why_kept: Flail leaflet secondary to recent tricuspid valve replacement

shortlist.label: Pacemaker-mediated tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Recent pacemaker placement and episodes of light-headedness and chest pain

shortlist.label: Infective endocarditis of the pulmonary valve
shortlist.why_kept: History of infective endocarditis and pulmonary valve vegetations

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and 3, suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive skin lesion around a stoma site with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis, possible association with underlying Crohn disease

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, clinical presentation of erosive skin lesion

shortlist.label: Pemphigus herpetiformis
shortlist.why_kept: Suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis, presence of IgG autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Pemphigus herpetiformis variant with IgG and C3 deposition
shortlist.why_kept: Direct immunofluorescence showing intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis, matching clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Anastrozole retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient recently started anastrozole, and fundus examination shows parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of crystalline deposits in the retina, consistent with Bietti crystalline retinopathy

shortlist.label: Tamoxifen retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although patient denied tamoxifen use, it's a known cause of crystalline retinopathy and should be considered

shortlist.label: Crystalline retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Direct match for the patient's fundus examination findings

shortlist.label: Cancer-associated retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of breast cancer, and cancer-associated retinopathy is a rare but possible cause of visual disturbance

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion

shortlist.label: angioma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology shows round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: rapidly growing, erythematous lesion with vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation and vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches histopathological features of round vascular channels and endothelial cell positivity for CD34 and CD31

shortlist.label: Atypical Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology findings of atypical compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction

shortlist.label: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large, dark brown patch with satellite lesions and areas of regression, consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus

shortlist.label: Dysplastic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular borders and variable coloration of the lesion, along with histopathology findings of atypical melanocytic proliferation

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although the gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, the presence of atypical features and areas of regression warrant consideration of melanoma

shortlist.label: Nevus of Ota
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopy findings of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas, which can be seen in nevus of Ota
